text:
Rachael: quick heads-up — after last night's runtime roll we're seeing structured outputs losing the 'contributors' array and a spike in hallucinations on summarization evals. Deploy tag rwood/runtime@v2.15.1, run-id run-20260318-02.
Samir: which rollout and can you paste repro steps?
Rachael: repro below:
```
python tools/repro.py --model redwood/gpt-xl-fp8 --quant per-layer-fp8 --batch 12 --prompt-file testcases/summaries_short.json --seed 7
```
Rachael: observed (truncated):
```
{"title":"Paper summary","summary":"...","contributors":null}
```
Rachael: expected contributors -> list of strings. Also seeing ~10-15% samples with extra invented sentences.
perf-bot: profiling summary uploaded: /artifacts/profiles/run-20260318-02/prof.json
- kernel_switches_per_request: 6.8 (baseline 2.1)
- kv_cache_hit_rate_longctx: 65% (baseline 90%)
- avg_token_latency: 40ms -> 60ms
perf-bot: flame excerpt:
```
kernel_selector -> fp8_perlayer_selector
fp8_perlayer_selector -> fp8_matmul_path
fp8_matmul_path -> cuda_gemm_fast
```
Leo: sounds like calibration sensitivity + batcher distribution change. per-layer FP8 scale drift can push softmax/ln ranges out of calibration and cause token drift -> hallucinations / missing schema fields.
Samir: saw warnings in calibrator logs: "/artifacts/calib/run-20260317-23/calib.log" shows: \"WARN: scale underflow at layer 17, effective range too small\" and \"quantizer: low dynamic range detected\".
Samir: theory: the adaptive batcher changed padding and pad-trimming behavior so activation percentiles shifted; per-layer calibrator picked tighter scales that aren't robust to the new batching regime.
Maria: did we try disabling the adaptive batcher in canary? any diff?
Rachael: yes — flipped canary to legacy batcher at 03:40 UTC for the affected model group; error rate fell back to baseline within one deploy window. :thumbsup: Ops rolled Dedicated to fallback profile (mixed-int8) at 04:05 UTC and customer incidents dropped.
Samir: repro locally with same seed, repro rate ~58% on my dev cluster.
Samir: mitigation proposal: clamp per-layer FP8 scales using a high percentile (e.g., 99.9%) and add a stability check: if per-layer scale variance > threshold, force mixed-int8 for that layer. I'll draft a patch + telemetry.
Samir: PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8499 (WIP) — adds conservative clamping + per-layer variance metric.
Leo: also add an eval regression test that asserts required keys present in structured outputs and a token-drift regression metric. Put failing sample in tests/evals/regressions/20260318-perlayer-fp8-missing-contributors.json.
Maria: ops request: add a canary rollout for per-layer-fp8 that runs on 2% of traffic with continuous eval; if regression rate > 2.5% auto-fallback to mixed-int8. Can we add alerting?
Samir: yes — will add rollout policy and alert automation. Also enabling extra telemetry for per-layer scale percentiles and kernel_switch count in next profile.
Rachael: assignments: Samir -> implement clamp + PR; Leo -> add eval test + failing sample; Maria -> canary + rollout policy + alert; Rachael -> release note + postmortem writeup. Target hotfix to prod by EOD today. @Samir :eyes: 
perf-bot: created perf/5831 and linked to /issues/5831. Hooked to #eng-runtime-triage.
Rachael: thanks all. keep updates short in this thread. :white_check_mark:
